title: Coefficient-normalized point insertion compositors on entire strict systems
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, $R$ its valuation ring, $\varpi$ a uniformizer, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, choose small representatives of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $h:s\xrightarrow{\sim}s$ be any scheme automorphism. Set $B_n=(A_n)_s$ and $\widehat R_s=\lim_nB_n$, with projections $\pi_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\mathscr S_s$ be the abelian category of sequences of $B_n$-module sheaves with $B_{n+1}$-linear transitions $v_n:M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{B_{n+1}\to B_n}M_n$; its morphisms commute with these transitions [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $U:\mathscr S_s\to\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(\widehat R_s))$ for levelwise scalar restriction [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Let $F_r=(h^r)^{-1}$ on completed modules, with scalars transported by the canonical coefficient maps $c_{r,\widehat R}:F_r\widehat R_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat R_s$, and let $G_r$ be levelwise inverse image on $\mathscr S_s$ [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. The same notation denotes their termwise actions on complexes and their exact induced functors on ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $F_r^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ for levelwise $F_r$ on completed-module towers. At finite level use the specified isomorphisms $j_{r,M}:F_rM\xrightarrow{\sim}(h^r)^*M$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, of part (a) of the inverse-image comparison.

For $m\geq1$, the canonical site compositor induces natural module and whole-system compositors $d_m:F_1F_m\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{m+1}$ and $t_m:G_1G_m\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{m+1}$. In site-reindexing coordinates they are the identity on every section. For $D=B_n$ and $D=\widehat R_s$, their coefficient normalization is
$$c_{m+1,D}\circ d_{m,D}=c_{1,D}\circ F_1(c_{m,D}),\qquad \pi_n c_{r,\widehat R}=c_{r,B_n}F_r(\pi_n).$$
There are sectionwise identity natural isomorphisms $b_r:F_r^{\mathrm{Tow}}U\xrightarrow{\sim}UG_r$, compatible with all original transitions, and
$$b_{m+1,M}\circ d^{\mathrm{Tow}}_{m,UM}=U(t_{m,M})\circ b_{1,G_mM}\circ F_1^{\mathrm{Tow}}(b_{m,M}).$$
Through $j_r$, the finite compositor is the inverse of the specified module-pullback compositor [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]; on tensor-unit insertions it sends $(x\otimes1)\otimes1$ to $x\otimes1$.

Let $\Gamma_\bullet$ be levelwise final-object sections and scalar restriction to $R$, retaining all transitions [def-trf-coefficient-tower-operations, lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. For every unbounded strict system complex $M$ and $r\geq1$, let $u_{r,M}:\Gamma_\bullet M\to\Gamma_\bullet G_rM$ be the degreewise restriction along $h^r$, inverse-image colimit insertion, sheafification, and, in the finite pullback presentation, insertion $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport, lem-trf-point-sheaf-insertion-calculus]. Then these are natural $R$-linear chain maps of whole towers, and
$$u_{m+1,M}=\Gamma_\bullet(t_{m,M})\circ u_{1,G_mM}\circ u_{m,M}.$$
In particular, both paths on a transition have value $v_n(x)\otimes\rho_n(1)=v_n(x)\otimes1$, where $\rho_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$ is coefficient reduction, and both commute with differentials. Their localizations $I_r$ satisfy
$$I_{m+1,C}=\Gamma_\bullet(t_{m,C})\circ I_{1,G_mC}\circ I_{m,C},\qquad C\in D(\mathscr S_s),$$
naturally for every derived system morphism. No cartesianness, normalization, boundedness, constructibility or Tor-amplitude hypothesis on $M$ or $C$ is imposed.

proof.text: For finite coefficients use uniqueness of the constant-normalized sectionwise comparison. Precompose the candidate composite with the inverse ring compositor; naturality of the constant sheafification unit and normalization of the two coefficient maps show that it fixes constants. For completed coefficients, the defining limit lift proves the projection formula. Project the composition identity to each finite ring, use naturality of the ring compositor and the finite identity, and use limit.hom_ext. This proves CoefficientLaws without an additional hypothesis. Use [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] and [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit].

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-point-system-normalized-comparisons] to CoefficientLaws to obtain the normalized d,t,b,j and their section, restriction, tensor and transition laws. Apply [lem-trf-point-system-strict-insertions] to the section laws to obtain u and its tower composition identity. Degreewise extensionality of the actual complexInsertion construction proves the chain identity from the tower identity. Update only the u field of Maps.

source.place: Tags 03CB and 0H7J; the explicit sectionwise coefficient-system refinement in the proof of lem-trf-point-system-insertion-composition (steps 1–6).

proof.text: The fixed data and exactness theorems are [def-trf-point-system-insertion-data]. Lift each chain insertion through the fully faithful universal property on natural transformations [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], using the exact derived functors already specified. The liftNatTrans component formula proves its required factorization. To prove composition, compare the natural transformations after precomposing with Q and cancel their invertible factorization maps. The specified derived compositor formula, naturality of insertion and of sections factorization, and the chain composition identity give equality. Localization.natTrans_ext then gives equality on all derived objects and morphisms. Update only I; the other laws do not use that field.

No SGA is cited. Step 1: lem-sfb (1) with W=(s,h^r) gives the reindexing model G(U,h^r u), and its hypothesis holds because an isomorphism is weakly etale; the generator node's composite index (graph with graph gives the graph of h^{m+1}) makes the compositor the identity in these coordinates. Step 2: I recomputed the finite identity c_{m+1}d_m=c_1F_1(c_m) from lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition with (h,h^m) and d_m equal to the inverse of alpha, and the completed identity by projecting with pi_n, using the definitional clause pi_m c=c_{A_m}g^{-1}(pi_m) and sectionwise limits. Step 3 is elementary and the two scalar actions agree by inverting step 2. Step 4: the hypothesis on the composite coefficient map of the tensor-composition node holds by step 2, its formula sends (x⊗1)⊗1 to d_m(x)⊗1, and the derived composition node specifies the termwise comparison. Step 5 handles the semilinear transitions through underlying abelian maps and balanced tensors, not through A_s-linear naturality. Step 6 is elementary. Step 7 uses exactness plus parts (1)-(3) of the localization universal property, with no claim that evaluations detect equality. Small cases checked: h=id, zero transitions, n=1, repeated powers. Not duplicates: lem-trf-point-transport-composition is only the finite, bounded, Frobenius analogue, and the parent cites the item only in its step 1. The declared tool uses are generic tools and accepted. Minor: the report mentions a citations.json that is not in the commit. No changes made.
